result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

The choice comes down to whether you prioritise ease of use and polished team sharing, or affordability and value.

My overall recommendation is **1Password for ease of use, Bitwarden for best value**\.

## Best password managers for small teams

![1Password 8 - Password Manager | iOS Icon Gallery](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/3kd4HdLTXZdmtixhaDTzQbLhY932F3n1KtDabTh3csuQ5kx3v8pe4UfA6fm4Alx6vDhb5RbcUp-yj7ihV4oAHDtOLoNF1yB5dnrTRaN3jToumhO0CjpLWn0JUnHcRdbHbaRgee0MTORW3RMau8EPoSOkRgMSt1RgQVQsBBo-M-6b-D4x5tzojsYy2O8rDKan?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall for usability)

- Excellent shared vaults and team permissions.
- Easy for non-technical staff.
- Strong admin controls and security monitoring.
- Good onboarding and offboarding.
  
  Business: approximately US\$8.99/user/month. Teams Starter Pack: US\$24.95/month for 10 users.
  
  [1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![‎Bitwarden App - App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/x38pyi5v1Vy6Zs97qz8ZgS0U3TY6bP46EZUol0vjWY-QJEsjpBL1sBYpo0AxExRZj59SXzc9D5J1hCMKpLCQRKtRmi0IYkc0CeiDQsrny4xPWuRz2OGsqZ9tyuMm4GtN5vMAwBBf6hXgHDHMP9_wXSBVttW9bXO5pQrWG4hhS-RxRNQIRTsbPrqb3y45Jv-M?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Open-source password manager.
- Shared collections and team access.
- Good administrative and audit features.
- Excellent value as the team grows.
  
  Teams: approximately US\$4/user/month annually.
  
  [Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![‎Keeper Password Manager App - App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6YqDIYCwAfpd6GObzC-G1I_Ae64PhD3Adg6yFTCDbBzmw2aNf2KsneQTuxazrol31Rc6ACKK3x9Eh1luvNAHDI1r711RPuAeW2f0aAFmjVsqzUYe4jhRFTDwXTW7NUhBUV3qqwhS9yrU3ZD-hUKGwId-qbRcNIdL4KiaJcX6Q-NTBSa05phiAGYremJ0qUvL?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Good admin console.
- Shared team folders.
- Strong access-management capabilities.
- Worth considering for security-conscious businesses.
  
  Entry pricing starts around US\$2/user/month for eligible small teams.
  
  [Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![Dashlane Password Manager - Productivity App | MWM](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/sjKEnc0-fPSrNqcxg632k2LsBv013jUcwYRRRFBtcM4jJvhfaV4R-pujj7qAehiPzT1cTFXTzWEXX9oHlGzAptfQkRhbi8qP8iQ0988C9QxscIXoPYcuBcOyQb2Af9AH8UZ94UR2tMHYRyo1y8r8JALEVHUzBLdiVqEL6adsEykVdzYzUhWmkr_9_-vfGxYV?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Dashlane**

- Polished interface.
- Password health monitoring.
- Security alerts and administrative policies.
- Good for businesses wanting additional credential-risk visibility.
  
  [Dashlane business plans](https://www.dashlane.com/business)

## Quick comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden | Keeper |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Shared passwords | Excellent | Excellent | Excellent |
| Team permissions | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Ease of use | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Value for money | Good | Excellent | Excellent |
| Small-team suitability | Excellent | Excellent | Good |


These are qualitative comparisons; exact features depend on subscription tier. Pricing above is in USD, generally billed annually. Check Australian pricing at checkout. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cybercred.com.au](https://cybercred.com.au/articles/password-managers-compared-for-small-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.softwarecompare.net](https://www.softwarecompare.net/comparison/best-password-manager-for-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for in a team password manager

Regardless of which one you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults** – securely share company credentials without sending passwords over Slack or email.
2. **Individual accounts** – every employee has their own login.
3. **Role-based permissions** – control who can access finance, HR, infrastructure and general accounts.
4. **Easy offboarding** – revoke access immediately when someone leaves.
5. **MFA** – require multi-factor authentication.
6. **Audit logs** – see relevant account and administrative activity.

## My recommendation

I'd shortlist 1Password and Bitwarden, trial both and see which your team finds easier to use.

One question that would help me make a more definite recommendation\:

**How many people are in your team?**

For example, a 3–5 person business has quite different needs from a 20–30 person company. I can narrow it down based on team size, cost and the level of security administration you need.
